fields.value: Bound owned-host disk growth (track/, programs/) and add explicit cleanup

Problem: Long-lived owned SSH hosts (such as `mini-r2`) still accumulate unbounded disk usage across three directories that PR #151 (`5e038f`) left outside its scope:
1. `~/.etude/track/<run>/` — the courier's local resume cache (`src/etude/launch/worker/courier.py`) on bucket-backed owned hosts.
2. `~/.etude/programs/<digest>/` — installed client environments (~200 MB per client upgrade) with no eviction of old digests (`src/etude/launch/ssh_boot.py`).
3. Pure-SSH session `outputs/` and logs — intentionally kept after attempts finish because the host disk is the only copy (`src/etude/launch/worker/attempts.py`), with no user command to reclaim them once no longer needed.

Outcome: Owned hosts stay bounded over hundreds of runs and upgrades without manual `rm`:
- Confirmed bucket-backed `track/` directories and old `programs/<digest>/` environments are evicted under a clear retention policy/budget.
- An explicit command (e.g., `etude machine clean NAME`) lets operators reclaim pure-SSH outputs/logs and stale host state intentionally without silent data loss.

Done when:
- Repeated runs and client upgrades on an owned host do not grow `~/.etude/track/` or `~/.etude/programs/` without bound (covered by deterministic tests without inducing load).
- Unconfirmed bucket deliveries and pure-SSH outputs are never deleted silently; explicit cleanup removes only settled/confirmed artifacts and reports what it freed.

Overlap & constraints:
- Builds on PR #151 (`5e038f`, touching `worker/courier.py`, `worker/attempts.py`, `ssh_boot.py`, `docs/launcher.md`), which already deletes attempt working trees before `finished.json` and removes confirmed bucket-backed session payloads/outputs.
- Keep one cache/budget owner; consequential deletion of pure-SSH outputs must stay explicit.
